why: An LIS where the previous value must lie in [x - k, x - 1]: the DP needs 'max over a value range', so compress values and keep a max segment tree indexed by value rank, querying the window and updating the point for x.
hints: Patience sorting does not handle the difference limit. Write the plain DP first: best[x] = 1 + max best[v] over earlier v with x - k <= v < x.
That max is over a contiguous range of values. Index a structure by value: compress the values to ranks and find the rank window with two binary searches.
Scan arr; for each x query the max on ranks [rank(x - k), rank(x) - 1], add 1, and raise position rank(x) to that value. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Strictly increasing: equal values cannot follow each other, so the window ends at x - 1.
k = 0 means no element can follow another; the answer is 1.
Update with max, since an equal value seen later may give a longer chain.
statement:
Given a non-empty integer array arr and a non-negative integer k, return the maximum length of a subsequence that satisfies all of the following:

  • It keeps the original order of the chosen elements.
  • It is strictly increasing.
  • Every two adjacent chosen elements differ by at most k.

Example: arr = [7,1,4,5,8,8,10,6,7,7,7,8], k = 4. The subsequence [1,4,5,6,7,8] is strictly increasing and its adjacent differences 3, 1, 1, 1, 1 are all at most 4, so the answer is 6.
